questions.question: Compare a threat and an attack as security concepts, and contrast how misuse-based and anomaly-based detection models each counter them, noting one strength and one weakness of each model.

marking_points.point: A threat is only a potential violation of security, not an actual one.
marking_points.quote: A threat is a                                                          “potential” violation of                                                                    security

marking_points.point: An attack is the actual violation of security, i.e. the realised exploitation.
marking_points.quote: Attacks: The actual                                                                               violation of security

marking_points.point: Misuse detection represents attacks as patterns or signatures so that variations of the same attack can be recognised.
marking_points.quote: there are ways to represent attacks in the form of a pattern or a signature so that even variations of the same attack can be detected

marking_points.point: A weakness of misuse detection is that it is of little use against unknown attack methods.
marking_points.quote: They can detect many or all known attack patterns, but they are of little use for unknown attack methods.

marking_points.point: A strength of predictive-pattern anomaly detection is that rule-based sequential patterns can detect anomalous activities that traditional methods struggled with.
marking_points.quote: Rule based sequential patterns can detect anomalous activities that were difficult with traditional methods.

marking_points.point: A weakness of predictive-pattern anomaly detection is that intrusion scenarios not described by the rules will not be flagged.
marking_points.quote: The problem is that some intrusion scenarios that are not described by the rules will not be flaged intrusive.
